control_flags.objectives: The subsections beneath a requirement whose lead-in states the duty; each is required unless the lead-in makes them a choice.

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable requirements that are implemented. The Act defines no score; this percentage is an HCG measure of progress.

rules.summary: A requirement is met only when every element it lists is met.

The Act applies to a business with annual revenue of $25 million or more that does business in Utah or targets Utah residents and either controls or processes personal data of 100,000 or more consumers a year, or earns over 50% of gross revenue from selling personal data of 25,000 or more consumers.
rules.quote: has annual revenue of $25,000,000 or more;

rules.summary: A consumer request is acted on, and the consumer told of the action, within 45 days of receipt; the period may be extended once by 45 days.
rules.quote: Within 45 days after the day on which a controller receives a request to exercise a right, the controller shall:

rules.summary: At least 30 days before enforcement the attorney general gives written notice; a violation cured within that period, with a written statement, is not pursued.
rules.quote: At least 30 days before the day on which the attorney general initiates an enforcement action against a controller or processor, the attorney general shall provide the controller or processor:

consequences.summary: A violation not cured after notice can lead to actual damages to consumers and up to $7,500 for each violation, recovered by the attorney general.

glossary.definition: The Utah Consumer Privacy Act, Utah's comprehensive consumer privacy law, in force since 31 December 2023.
The person that, alone or jointly with others, determines the purpose and means of processing personal data.
A person that processes personal data on behalf of a controller.

Personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, religious beliefs, health diagnosis, sexual orientation, citizenship or immigration status; genetic or biometric data used to identify a person; data of a known child; and precise geolocation data.
Personal data that cannot be attributed to a specific individual without additional information that is kept separately under appropriate safeguards.
